conventions.convention: Topologicality concerns every declared complete admissible correlator, with background and boundary data fixed, under decorated isotopies avoiding all other insertions. It is not inferred from a label or fusion table.
Defect supports are smooth embedded manifolds without boundary, closed in the spacetime interior. Networks additionally specify strata, incidence, decorations, and ordered junction data.
An interface is directed from the negative-side model to the positive-side model. Fusion I12 ⋆ I01 has source T0 and target T2.
Fusion requires convergence of every declared complete correlator in a specified common Hausdorff value space, together with limiting normalization and junction data.
An internal invertible symmetry requires the same complete source and target model, two-sided identity fusion, and insertion/background bijections preserving all correlators.

The Z2 model uses H=0, arbitrary density matrices, dimensionless insertion matrices, chronological products with later factors on the left, and simultaneous conjugation of insertions and boundary density matrices.

Normalized interface amplitudes admit only boundary pairs with nonzero empty-list amplitude; reverse-pair fusion additionally requires a nonzero identity-interface normalization limit. Natural units have hbar=1 and Euclidean times have inverse-energy units.

load_bearing.statement: The insertion is topological in T if, for every complete admissible input containing the selected network and every decorated isotopy disjoint from all other insertion data, C_T(b;D0;X1,…,Xn)=C_T(b;D1;X1,…,Xn).

An endodefect is an invertible symmetry interface only if a two-sided inverse exists under the stated fusion operation, both composites equal the transparent identity in all declared correlators, and its induced insertion and background/boundary bijections are automorphisms preserving correlators. A topological interface between distinct source and target models is not an internal symmetry of either model.

published_dependencies.used_for: Opened as a cited mathematical supplier of the contextual prerequisite def-aqft-noninvertible-defect-fusion: finite semisimple tensor versus multitensor categories. Neither assigned physical definition infers realization from this abstract data.
Opened as a cited supplier of the fusion-mathematics prerequisite to check associator direction, pentagon, and triangle conventions.

seams_checked.note: Contextual page prerequisite. Abstract fusion data expressly do not construct physical defects; the assigned definitions independently require model-defined insertions and correlators. The associator pentagon diagram matches its stated directions.
Contextual page prerequisite only. The assigned definitions do not use BPS saturation, assert supersymmetry, or infer physical defect existence from the massive-rest-fiber statements.

The symmetry definition retains closed embedded supports, complete insertion data, decorated isotopy invariance, and simultaneous background/boundary covariance. Group fusion and crossing compatibility are additional supplied conditions.

The finite-regulator definition explicitly supplies complete network correlators and requires intermediate-support correlators and comparison maps for smooth isotopies. Ordinary no-defect sums alone are not claimed to establish topologicality.

The realization explicitly restricts topologicality to declared finite-lattice line slides and proves their invariance inside complete network contractions. It expressly makes no arbitrary smooth-continuum isotopy claim.

The consumer uses the general defect-insertion and stratified-network clauses. It explicitly says the half-BPS surface defect need not be topological and treats the two open half-planes as strata of one closed network rather than separate closed defects.
